cohort: 460 low-risk pregnant women attending antenatal clinics in El-Beheira Governorate, Egypt.
finding: The prevalence of Fear of Childbirth (FOC) among Egyptian pregnant women was high, with 70.4% displaying some degree of fear and 11.3% exhibiting severe FOC, significantly associated with younger age, nulliparity, unplanned pregnancy, negative previous birth experiences, preference for cesarean delivery, and lower childbirth self-efficacy.
mod_finding: Preference for cesarean delivery was identified as a key determinant associated with greater fear of childbirth.
